header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Rate schedule hand-transcribed from the 2026 D-40ES booklet (Rev. 03/2026) and matches OTR's rate page (unchanged since tax year 2022; one schedule for all filing statuses); sha256 is of the canonical body. Brackets are ENACTED and verified. File is marked projected because the 2026 STANDARD DEDUCTION dollar amounts could not be verified. The 2026 D-40ES worksheet (issued March 2026) used the federal OBBBA amounts ($16,100 single/MFS, $24,150 HoH, $32,200 joint; additional $1,650 married / $2,050 unmarried for age 65+ or blind). However, DC decoupled from the OBBBA standard deduction for 2025 ($15,000 single/MFS, $22,500 HoH, $30,000 joint per the 2025 D-40 booklet), and the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Support Act of 2026 (emergency act B26-0724 in effect but expiring November 11, 2026; permanent act B26-0661 in congressional review) keeps DC decoupled through tax year 2029: the DC standard deduction for 2026-2029 is the tax-year-2025 amount with an annual cost-of-living adjustment, returning to the federal amount for tax years after 2029 (CFO fiscal impact statement; EY Tax News 2026-1962). OTR had not published the COLA-adjusted 2026 figures at retrieval. Values encoded are the statutory 2025 base amounts ($15,000 / $30,000 / $15,000 / $22,500), i.e. a floor - the actual 2026 amounts should be a few hundred dollars higher (and would be $16,100/$32,200/$24,150 if the permanent act were disapproved by Congress). seniorExtraDeduction is the additional standard deduction for age 65+ at the tax-year-2025 DC amount for married filers ($1,600; $2,000 if single/HoH); the 2026 figure is likewise unverified. The Budget Support Act allows DC deductions for tips, overtime and car-loan interest from 2026; treatment of the OBBBA senior deduction for 2026 was not verified. Social Security and tier 1 railroad retirement benefits are fully subtracted. No general pension/IRA exclusion (a $3,000 exclusion remains only for certain survivor annuitants 62+; up to $10,000 exclusion for permanently disabled residents with low income). No capital gains preference. Rate brackets are not inflation-indexed; the standard deduction is. No separate local income tax.
